title: Down To The Wire For EU Transfer Spending
text:
Down To The Wire For EU Transfer Spending

August Gudmundsson

Gavekal Research | 26 Nov 2026

The European Union’s poorer member states look set to lose out in the bloc’s next long-term budget. Negotiations over the 2028-34 Multiannual Financial Framework enter a decisive phase at this week’s special European Council summit, with Brussels seeking to fund new strategic priorities while repaying pandemic-related debt. The European Commission hopes to secure a political agreement by year-end, ahead of national European elections in 2027. Whatever the eventual compromise, the likely squeeze on transfers will put pressure on areas historically reliant on EU funding, notably infrastructure investment in Eastern Europe.The headline budget increase is deceptive. The Commission’s original proposal envisages spending of €1.98trn for 2028-34, a 59% nominal increase. This equates to 1.26% of EU gross national income, up from 1.13% in the previous budget. (GNI is used rather than GDP as it better reflects member states’ ability to pay.) Yet much of the increase is accounted for by €168bn in debt repayments under the NextGenerationEU pandemic recovery package. Stripping out debt repayments, the core budget rises only marginally to 1.15% of GNI.
